approved_scope.title: Hash a change's clean delivery files one blob at a time so reopen does not overflow a single Git read on large affected paths
approved_scope.description: Hash a change's clean delivery files one blob at a time so reopen does not overflow a single Git read on large affected paths
acceptance_criteria: Each clean blob is still bounded by MAX_GIT_EVIDENCE_PAYLOAD_BYTES, and a blob over it is refused by name; the path-count bound and the Git read deadline are unchanged, and every other caller of inspect_git_candidates keeps both of its caps.
Failing tests first: each new test fails on main f7180c34 and passes after the change; no gate, timeout or assertion is loosened.

SHIP-6 (REQ-change-144): reopen of a stale accepted change whose clean affected files exceed one git cat-file --batch read, with or without an acceptance manifest, no longer fails with "`git cat-file --batch` output exceeds deterministic bounds"; a test-only seam shrinks the cap so the test runs on small fixtures.

The acceptance manifest and the acceptance input digest are byte-identical to the ones the whole-scope read produced, for clean, modified, symlinked, deleted and executable files, an LFS pointer and the sequence ledger, so every recorded manifest and digest still matches.
The accepted-input validation behind change status and the archive preflight builds that evidence the same way.

answers.constraints: Leif approved the plan through orc t18 ('Capture all + approve design', 2026-11-06): no new HI, SHIP-6 covers it; REQ-change-144 claimed by the orc; #976. The one bound that changes is named for approval: these two evidence builders lose their all-at-once total-bytes cap and keep a per-blob cap of the same size (memory stays bounded by one blob). No other gate, bound, timeout or assertion is loosened. Recorded manifests and digests must stay byte-identical. No tag, release or crates.io publish.
